properties.statement: The failed and partially failed congruence-family approaches all operate through fixed-modulus congruence identities whose eliminating power is structurally confined to quadratic non-residues, so their coverage halts at the same quadratic-residue survivor classes rather than degrading gradually.

supporting_passages.quote: these identities are keyed to fixed moduli
Blocked by the quadratic-reciprocity obstruction, not by search effort.
no finite covering eliminates quadratic-residue classes
exceptional set is thin but infinite and protected by the QR wall
every failed family here preserves the quadratic-residue wall.

properties.preserved_distinctions: It does not merge the structurally different uses of congruence identities: es-01 is class-local and constructive (one identity per residue class, classes never coupled), es-12 is global and form-first (Type A/B forms chosen to avoid quadratic residues, then assembled toward coverage), and es-10 is an aggregate density bound over many classes rather than a coverage claim. es-08 is not a construction at all but the meta-level diagnosis of the shared confinement.
properties.contrast_check: The property does not cleanly discriminate: the partial-success covering-system attempt (es-02) is also built from these identities and stalls on the same wall ('no finite covering built from these identities can catch the quadratic-residue classes'). However, the other partial successes (es-03 divisor factorization, es-04 Type I/II classification, es-06 two-fraction bounds, es-07 computational verification) do not depend on fixed-modulus identity solvability, and es-07 even dispatches QR primes within its finite range, so the confinement tracks the identity-carrying mechanism rather than the problem as a whole.
properties.falsification: Exhibiting, within the corpus's terms, a fixed-modulus congruence identity or identity-built covering that eliminates a quadratic-residue class (or a note recording that one of these approaches stalled somewhere other than the QR survivor classes) would refute the property.

properties.statement: Several partially failed approaches perform an existential re-organization of the problem — characterizing, unifying, or obstructing — that preserves known solution structure but adds no positivity, so no new existence is forced on the survivor classes.

supporting_passages.quote: Abstraction/transfer move; compression without added positivity.
constraint geometry of solutions rather than constructing them for a fixed `n`.
an obstruction is not a solution

properties.preserved_distinctions: The property does not merge the distinct operations involved: es-09 re-represents at a higher abstraction level (algebraic lift of parameterizations onto one variety), es-11 works at ground level on algebraic relations and symmetries among denominators, and es-08 reasons about the space of methods to prove a negative structural fact. Their operators (lift/unification vs constraint analysis vs reciprocity obstruction) and abstraction levels remain different; they share only the existential, non-constructive posture with zero added existence.
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success Type I/II classification (es-04) also 'characterizes what solutions *must* look like without constructing them', so an existential characterizing posture alone is present on the partial-success side too. The discriminating refinement is that the partially failed notes explicitly record that the re-organization contributed no positivity ('not a new source of existence'), whereas es-04 is credited as a productive foundation for the counting and averaging work.
properties.falsification: A note showing that one of these re-organization moves by itself produced a new existence result (positivity) for quadratic-residue survivor primes — e.g., the variety lift forcing a solution on a previously uncovered class — would refute the property.

properties.statement: The two density/averaging approaches share an intrinsically capped coverage profile: they prove strong 'almost all' statements whose gap to 'all n' is a structural feature of the method (polylogarithmic average growth, exceptional-set density with a nonzero floor), not a shortfall of effort.

supporting_passages.quote: Its boundary is intrinsic to the method: the average grows only polylogarithmically.
prime has few solutions, and rare primes could in principle have none.
the number of exceptional `n` up to `N` is small

properties.preserved_distinctions: It does not collapse the two mechanisms: es-05 is probabilistic in posture, averaging a solution-count function over an ensemble of primes with sieve machinery (Bombieri–Vinogradov, Brun–Titchmarsh), while es-10 is deterministic, assembling identity-bearing congruence classes and bounding the leftover. One measures typical solution abundance, the other measures thinness of the unsolved set; they cap out for different structural reasons (slow average growth vs reciprocity-protected survivors).
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success two-fraction bounds (es-06) also yield results holding 'for almost all primes' that degrade at quadratic-residue primes, so 'almost all coverage' alone does not discriminate. What separates the partially failed pair is the recorded intrinsic impossibility of upgrade: es-05 states its bound 'cannot' be upgraded because the growth is only polylog, and es-10 states its density can never reach zero; es-06 carries no such internal ceiling claim.
properties.falsification: Evidence that either method's bound can be upgraded within its own machinery to an empty exceptional set — e.g., a note showing polynomial rather than polylog average growth, or a class assembly whose leftover density provably reaches zero — would refute the property.
